title: Educate, Agitate, Organize: The Nagpur Clarion Call
summary: Ambedkar explained the profound philosophical sequence of his three mantras: knowledge awakens dignity, agitation shatters submission, and organization creates unconquerable collective power.
keywords: Educate, Agitate, Organize: The Nagpur Clarion Call
full_text:
In July 1942, seventy-five thousand delegates gathered under monsoon clouds in Nagpur for the All-India Depressed Classes Conference.

Dr. Ambedkar, currently serving as Member for Labour in the Viceroy's Executive Council, stepped to the microphone.

Looking across the vast expanse of working-class citizens, he posed a piercing question:
"Comrades! Why have you languished as slaves for generations?
Are your oppressors born with extra limbs? Does different blood flow through their veins?
No! You remain in chains because of three fatal deficiencies:
First: You lack education.
Second: You lack the divine discontent to revolt against injustice.
Third: You are fractured into a hundred sub-castes devoid of unity!

To break this curse, I give you three sacred commandments:

My first command: **Educate!**
Educate yourselves and educate your children! Even if you must starve, send your daughters and sons to school. Education is the milk of the tigress; whoever drinks it will roar!

My second command: **Agitate!**
Do not accept your misery as karma or fate! Do not bow your head like sheep before cruelty. Awake, arise, and agitate against every humiliation! Rights are never gifted; they must be conquered!

My third command: **Organize!**
Cast aside your petty divisions! If you remain isolated fingers, the oppressor will snap you one by one. But if those five fingers clench together into a solitary iron fist... that fist can shatter the mightiest fortress of oppression on earth!"

The gathering erupted into an ocean of roars: "Babasaheb Zindabad!"

Those three words—**Educate, Agitate, Organize**—became the eternal manifesto of social revolution, transforming millions from submissive laborers into proud architects of their own destiny.
moral: Knowledge, courage, and solidarity are the three essential pillars of any genuine movement for human liberation.
